Choose a pass in this partially observed Football Chess position. Maximize the probability that your team keeps possession after the next defensive challenge. All three passes are legal and arrive for certain. Your team then holds position. The defense takes a legal tackle whenever one is available.

In this rule variant only the rook has protection: if tackled it retains possession with probability 75%. Any other tackled receiver loses possession. Any receiver that cannot be tackled keeps possession. These rules specify all receiver abilities.

Pitch coordinates (files a-n, ranks 1-17). Your side is white and your queen has the ball.
Your players: bishop h14, keeper i1, knight h11, queen e11, rook j6.
Visible opposing players: bishop i13, keeper h17, pawn b15, queen l7, rook j7.

One opposing pawn is hidden. Before receiving the scout report, its two possible squares are equally likely. On j9 the knight is safe (no legal tackle). On k9 the knight is exposed (a legal tackle exists). Both squares leave the rook and the bishop exposed. These conditional tackle outcomes are given.

The scout reports either SAFE or EXPOSED for the knight. In each of the two possible states the report is correct 60% of the time and gives the opposite report otherwise. The scout now reports: SAFE.

Choose one recipient:
1. knight on h11
2. rook on j6
3. bishop on h14
Return just its option number.
